title: YSR Aarogyasri 2026: Rs 5 Lakh Free Health Cover in AP
meta_description: YSR Aarogyasri AP 2026 - ₹5 lakh free cashless hospitalization for 1.42 crore families. 2,434 procedures, 30 categories. Check hospitals and eligibility.

hero.one_liner: ₹5 lakh cashless hospitalization for 1.42 crore AP families - 2,434 procedures covered at government and empanelled private hospitals. No premium for eligible families.

what_is_it: YSR Aarogyasri is Andhra Pradesh's flagship health insurance scheme providing free cashless hospitalization up to ₹5 lakh per family per year. Launched in 2007 by then CM Y.S. Rajasekhara Reddy, it covers over 1.42 crore families across the state. The scheme is managed by the Dr. YSR Aarogyasri Health Care Trust under the Department of Health, Medical & Family Welfare.

The scheme covers 2,434 procedures and surgeries across 30 categories - cardiac surgery, cancer treatment, orthopedic procedures, neurological care, renal dialysis, organ transplants, burn care, and more. Treatment is cashless at empanelled government and private hospitals. You walk in with your ration card and Aadhaar, and the hospital handles everything with the trust directly.

If you're eligible for both Aarogyasri and the Central Government's Ayushman Bharat (PMJAY), you get dual coverage - up to ₹10 lakh total per year (₹5 lakh from each). Hospitals can use whichever scheme covers the specific procedure, giving AP families significantly more protection than most other states.

All families with annual income below ₹5 lakh from all sources are eligible. White ration card holders are automatically enrolled - no separate registration needed. Emergency treatment does not require pre-authorization; hospitals treat first and seek approval later. For planned surgeries, pre-authorization is needed and typically takes 1-3 days.

extra_sections.heading: How to Get Treatment Under Aarogyasri - Step by Step

steps.title: Verify hospital is empanelled
steps.description: Before visiting, confirm the hospital accepts Aarogyasri. Check the list on ysraarogyasri.ap.gov.in or call 104. Government hospitals are automatically empanelled; private hospitals must be verified.

steps.title: Go to the Aarogyasri counter at the hospital
steps.description: Every empanelled hospital has a dedicated Aarogyasri registration counter. Bring your white ration card and Aadhaar card. The staff will verify your eligibility in the system (takes 15-30 minutes).

steps.title: Doctor examines and recommends treatment
steps.description: The hospital doctor examines you and determines if your condition requires hospitalization under a covered procedure. If yes, the hospital initiates the treatment process.

steps.title: Pre-authorization for planned surgery
steps.description: For non-emergency procedures, the hospital submits a pre-authorization request to the Aarogyasri Trust. Approval typically takes 1-3 days. Emergency cases skip this - treatment starts immediately, authorization happens later.

steps.title: Receive cashless treatment
steps.description: You're admitted and treated without paying anything out of pocket. All costs up to ₹5 lakh are billed directly to the Aarogyasri Trust by the hospital.

steps.title: Discharge - no bills
steps.description: After treatment, you're discharged without paying any hospital fees. The hospital settles everything with the Trust. If the hospital asks you to pay, complain immediately to 104.

extra_sections.heading: Aarogyasri vs Ayushman Bharat - Key Differences
What is NOT Covered Under Aarogyasri
content:
OPD and consultations

Only inpatient hospitalization is covered. Doctor consultations, outpatient visits, and routine check-ups are not included.

Cosmetic procedures

Aesthetic and cosmetic surgeries are excluded. Exception: reconstructive surgery after burns or accidents is covered.

Non-empanelled hospitals

Treatment at hospitals not on the Aarogyasri network is NOT covered. Always verify empanelment before admission.

Fertility treatments

IVF, IUI, surrogacy, and other fertility procedures are excluded.

Dental and orthodontic work

Routine dental procedures, braces, and dental implants are not covered.

Motor accident cases

If your condition is covered under motor vehicle insurance (third-party or own damage), that insurance is responsible - not Aarogyasri.

Outside medicines

Medicines purchased from pharmacies outside the hospital during treatment may not be reimbursed unless specifically prescribed and approved.

extra_sections.heading: How to Check if a Hospital is Empanelled
content: The safest way: Visit ysraarogyasri.ap.gov.in and use the 'Hospital Search' feature. Enter your district and city to see all empanelled hospitals in your area.
Call the 104 helpline - the staff can verify any hospital's empanelment status over the phone. Available 24/7.
Look for visible signs at the hospital: most empanelled hospitals display the Aarogyasri empanelment certificate and have a dedicated Aarogyasri counter near the entrance.

Government hospitals in AP are automatically empanelled. For private hospitals, ALWAYS verify before admission - not all private hospitals participate, and treatment at non-empanelled hospitals will not be covered.

extra_sections.heading: ₹5 lakh cover per family per year
extra_sections.content: YSR Aarogyasri covers 2,446 medical procedures including surgeries, therapies, and diagnostics. The ₹5 lakh limit is per family per year. For critical illnesses like cancer, kidney transplant, and cardiac surgery, an additional ₹5 lakh (total ₹10 lakh) is available under the enhanced package.

extra_sections.heading: Works with Ayushman Bharat
extra_sections.content: YSR Aarogyasri is integrated with PM-JAY (Ayushman Bharat) in Andhra Pradesh. If you have both cards, the hospital uses whichever scheme covers your specific treatment. The AP government tops up the Ayushman ₹5 lakh with additional state funds for procedures not covered under PM-JAY.

extra_sections.heading: Treatments and Procedures Covered Under YSR Aarogyasri
content: YSR Aarogyasri covers over 2,400 medical procedures across 1,000+ conditions spanning all major medical and surgical specialties. The coverage is among the most comprehensive of any state health insurance scheme in India.

Cardiac procedures including coronary artery bypass grafting, angioplasty with stent placement, valve replacement surgery, pacemaker implantation, and congenital heart defect corrections are fully covered. These procedures alone can cost Rs 2 lakh to Rs 6 lakh at private hospitals, making cardiac coverage the most financially impactful component of the scheme for beneficiaries.

Cancer treatment is covered end-to-end including diagnosis, surgery, chemotherapy, radiation therapy, and follow-up care. The scheme covers all common cancer types - breast, cervical, lung, oral, colorectal, blood cancers, and others. Given that cancer treatment costs in India can range from Rs 5 lakh to Rs 30 lakh depending on the type and stage, this coverage is potentially life-saving for families who would otherwise have no access to treatment.

Orthopedic surgeries including joint replacements (hip and knee), spinal surgeries, and fracture management with implants are covered. Neurosurgery procedures like brain tumor removal, spinal cord surgery, and treatment of cerebral hemorrhage fall under the scheme. Organ transplants including kidney transplant, liver transplant, and corneal transplant are also covered, though the availability of donor organs remains a separate challenge.

Other covered specialties include nephrology (dialysis and kidney disease management), urology, gastroenterology, ENT surgeries, ophthalmology (cataract surgery, retinal procedures), burns treatment, neonatal intensive care, and polytrauma management. The scheme also covers diagnostic procedures like CT scans, MRI scans, PET scans, and specialized blood tests when ordered as part of a covered treatment protocol.

extra_sections.heading: The Patient Journey - From Hospital Visit to Cashless Treatment
content: Understanding the step-by-step process of accessing YSR Aarogyasri benefits helps families navigate the system without delays or confusion. The process begins at an empaneled hospital and involves several verification stages.

Step 1: Visit any empaneled network hospital. You can find the nearest empaneled hospital through the Aarogyasri website, by calling the toll-free helpline 104, or by visiting your nearest Primary Health Centre which maintains a list. Government hospitals are automatically part of the network.

Step 2: At the hospital, present your Aarogyasri health card or white ration card to the Aarogyasri Help Desk. The desk verifies your eligibility through biometric authentication using your fingerprint against the Aadhaar database. If biometric verification fails due to fingerprint issues, the desk can use alternative identification methods.

Step 3: The treating doctor examines you and determines whether your condition requires a procedure covered under the scheme. If yes, the hospital submits a pre-authorization request to the Aarogyasri Trust through the online portal. This request includes your diagnosis, proposed treatment plan, estimated cost, and medical reports.

Step 4: The Aarogyasri Trust reviews the pre-authorization request. For emergency cases, approval is expedited within hours. For planned procedures, approval typically takes 24 to 72 hours. The trust may request additional medical documents or a second opinion before approving.

Step 5: Once approved, the treatment proceeds on a completely cashless basis. The hospital provides all treatment, medicines, surgical consumables, and post-operative care without charging the patient. The hospital bills the Aarogyasri Trust directly after treatment completion.

Step 6: Post-treatment follow-up visits are also covered for a specified period depending on the procedure. The hospital provides discharge instructions and a follow-up schedule, and subsequent visits within the covered follow-up period are free.

extra_sections.heading: Eligibility and Enrollment - Who Qualifies
content: YSR Aarogyasri is designed for below poverty line families and economically weaker sections in Andhra Pradesh. The eligibility is linked to the white ration card system - families holding white ration cards issued by the AP Civil Supplies Department are automatically eligible.

As of the latest expansion, approximately 1.42 crore families (roughly 87% of the state's population) are covered under the scheme, making it one of the most universally accessible health insurance programs in India. The high coverage percentage reflects the scheme's broad income thresholds compared to schemes in other states.

To check your eligibility, visit the official Aarogyasri website and enter your ration card number or Aadhaar number. The system will confirm whether your family is enrolled and display the names of all family members covered. If you hold a white ration card but are not showing as enrolled, visit your nearest Meeseva center or village secretariat to get your details updated in the system.

New white ration card holders are automatically added to the Aarogyasri database during periodic synchronization with the Civil Supplies Department records. However, if you recently received your white ration card and need immediate medical treatment, visit the Aarogyasri Help Desk at any empaneled hospital - they can expedite eligibility verification.

extra_sections.heading: YSR Aarogyasri vs PM-JAY - How They Work Together
content: Ayushman Bharat Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY) is the central government's health insurance scheme providing Rs 5 lakh coverage per family per year. Andhra Pradesh has integrated PM-JAY with its state scheme to create a more comprehensive coverage structure.

Under the integration, eligible families in AP receive the Rs 5 lakh PM-JAY coverage as the base layer. The state government adds its own funding through YSR Aarogyasri to provide additional coverage beyond the PM-JAY limit. In practice, this means AP families effectively have coverage exceeding the Rs 5 lakh limit for serious conditions that require expensive treatments.

The treatment package rates under the integrated scheme are determined by the state government and may differ from the PM-JAY national rates for the same procedures. AP has generally negotiated higher package rates for complex procedures like organ transplants and cancer treatment, which makes more private hospitals willing to participate in the network.

From the beneficiary's perspective, the integration is seamless. You do not need to carry separate cards or undergo different verification processes for PM-JAY and Aarogyasri. The single Aarogyasri health card serves both purposes, and the hospital manages the billing split between central and state funding internally.

extra_sections.heading: Emergency Treatment Rule
extra_sections.content: In genuine medical emergencies, any empaneled hospital must start treatment immediately without waiting for pre-authorization approval. The hospital can seek post-facto approval from the Aarogyasri Trust within 48 hours of emergency admission. If you or a family member needs emergency medical attention, go directly to the nearest empaneled hospital and inform them of your Aarogyasri eligibility. Do not delay seeking emergency care because of paperwork concerns - the scheme specifically mandates immediate treatment in life-threatening situations.

extra_sections.heading: Common Problems Beneficiaries Face and Solutions
content: The most frequently reported issue is private hospital staff claiming that a particular procedure is not covered under Aarogyasri when it actually is. This sometimes happens because hospitals prefer full-paying patients over scheme patients due to the lower reimbursement rates. If a hospital refuses treatment that you believe is covered, call the Aarogyasri helpline at 104 to verify coverage and report the hospital's behavior. You can also visit a different empaneled hospital for the same treatment.

Biometric verification failures are common among elderly patients and manual laborers whose fingerprints may be worn or unclear. In such cases, the hospital help desk should use alternative verification methods including iris scan or manual verification through Aadhaar demographic data. If the help desk refuses to try alternative methods, escalate to the hospital's Aarogyasri coordinator or call the helpline.

Delays in pre-authorization for planned procedures can extend beyond the expected 24 to 72 hours during peak periods or when the trust requests additional medical documentation. Keep all medical reports, test results, and doctor's prescriptions organized and readily available to avoid documentation-related delays. If pre-authorization is delayed beyond 5 working days, contact the District Coordinator of the Aarogyasri scheme for intervention.

Some beneficiaries report being asked to pay for medicines or consumables that should be included in the cashless treatment package. Under the scheme rules, the hospital is not permitted to charge patients for any component of the approved treatment package. If you are asked to pay, request a written explanation from the hospital and report it to the Aarogyasri Trust grievance cell.
For more details, see our guide on PM Suraksha Bima Yojana.

extra_sections.heading: Impact of YSR Aarogyasri on Healthcare in Andhra Pradesh
content: Since its inception, YSR Aarogyasri has fundamentally transformed healthcare access in Andhra Pradesh. The scheme has financed over 30 lakh medical procedures across its operational years, preventing catastrophic health expenditure for millions of families who would otherwise have been forced into debt or denied treatment.

The scheme has significantly expanded the private hospital network in tier-2 and tier-3 cities across AP. Towns like Tirupati, Vijayawada, Guntur, Kakinada, and Kurnool have seen new multi-specialty hospitals establish operations specifically to serve the Aarogyasri patient base. This has improved healthcare infrastructure access for the entire population, not just scheme beneficiaries.

Cardiac and cancer treatment outcomes have shown measurable improvement since the scheme's launch. Patients who previously could not afford bypass surgery or chemotherapy now receive these treatments at empaneled hospitals with quality standards monitored by the Aarogyasri Trust. The scheme's quality monitoring mechanism includes random audits of treated patients and clinical outcome tracking for major procedures.

The financial protection impact is most visible in rural AP where medical debt was historically the leading cause of families falling below the poverty line. Government data indicates that out-of-pocket health expenditure among Aarogyasri beneficiary families has decreased significantly since the scheme's expansion, though exact figures vary by study methodology.

extra_sections.heading: How to File Grievances and Escalate Issues
content: If you face any problems accessing Aarogyasri benefits, multiple grievance channels are available. The primary helpline is 104, available round the clock. You can also file complaints on the official Aarogyasri website's grievance portal by entering your ration card number and describing the issue. Each complaint receives a tracking number for follow-up.

For hospital-level issues like denial of treatment or demands for payment, approach the Aarogyasri Help Desk coordinator at the hospital first. If unresolved, contact the District Aarogyasri Coordinator whose office is usually located at the District Collector's office complex. District Coordinators have the authority to intervene directly with hospitals and expedite pre-authorizations.

The Aarogyasri Trust also conducts regular patient satisfaction surveys and hospital audits. Hospitals with repeated complaints face penalties including temporary suspension from the network or permanent de-empanelment. This quality enforcement mechanism protects beneficiaries and ensures hospitals maintain treatment standards.

extra_sections.heading: Planning for Medical Treatment Under Aarogyasri - Practical Tips
content: For planned surgeries, choose a hospital with a strong track record in your specific procedure. Ask the Aarogyasri Help Desk about the hospital's case volume and outcomes for the treatment you need. Hospitals that perform a procedure frequently generally have better outcomes and smoother processes.

Collect all medical reports, test results, and referral letters before visiting the empaneled hospital. Having complete documentation speeds up the pre-authorization process significantly. Missing reports are the most common cause of delays - hospitals often need to order repeat tests when patients arrive without prior diagnostic records.

If your condition requires ongoing treatment like dialysis or chemotherapy, confirm the entire treatment protocol coverage at the start. Some beneficiaries discover mid-treatment that certain sessions or drugs require separate pre-authorization, causing treatment gaps. Discussing the full treatment plan with the hospital's Aarogyasri coordinator before starting treatment prevents these interruptions.

For families in rural areas far from empaneled hospitals, the scheme provides transport reimbursement of Rs 200 to Rs 1,000 depending on the distance. Inquire about this benefit at the hospital help desk after your treatment. While the amount does not fully cover transportation costs for distant hospitals, it provides partial relief for families who must travel to district headquarters or cities for specialized care.

extra_sections.text: YSR Aarogyasri has turned the promise of universal healthcare from a political slogan into a functioning system where a farmer's family in Srikakulam can access the same cardiac surgery as a wealthy family in Hyderabad.

extra_sections.heading: Empaneled Hospital Network and Quality Standards
content: YSR Aarogyasri maintains a network of over 900 empaneled hospitals across Andhra Pradesh including both government and private institutions. The empanelment process requires hospitals to meet specific infrastructure, staffing, and quality benchmarks before they can treat scheme beneficiaries.

Private hospitals must have NABH accreditation or NABH entry-level certification to be empaneled for most surgical procedures. They must demonstrate adequate ICU beds, operation theaters, qualified specialist doctors on their payroll (not visiting consultants), and 24/7 emergency services. These requirements ensure that beneficiaries receive treatment at facilities that meet minimum quality standards rather than at under-equipped clinics.

The Aarogyasri Trust conducts periodic quality audits of empaneled hospitals. Audit teams review patient records, verify treatment outcomes, check infrastructure maintenance, and interview patients about their experience. Hospitals that fail audits receive warnings, and repeat failures lead to temporary suspension or permanent de-empanelment from the network.

Government district hospitals and teaching hospitals attached to medical colleges are automatically part of the network. These facilities handle a significant portion of Aarogyasri cases, particularly in districts where private hospital availability is limited. The scheme has incentivized several government hospitals to upgrade their infrastructure and specialist departments to handle the increased patient volume.

extra_sections.heading: Checking Empaneled Hospitals Near You
extra_sections.content: Visit the Aarogyasri website and navigate to the Hospital Network section to find empaneled hospitals in your district. You can filter by specialty - cardiac, cancer, orthopedic, or neurosurgery - to find hospitals equipped for your specific condition. The list includes hospital contact numbers and addresses. You can also call the 104 helpline and ask for hospital recommendations based on your location and medical need.

extra_sections.heading: Aarogyasri for Dialysis and Long-Term Treatment
content: Chronic kidney disease patients requiring regular dialysis sessions can access free treatment at Aarogyasri-empaneled dialysis centers. The scheme covers both hemodialysis and peritoneal dialysis including the cost of consumables, dialysis machine usage, and medications administered during the session. Patients typically require two to three sessions per week, and the cumulative annual cost can exceed Rs 3 to Rs 4 lakh - a burden that would be impossible for most BPL families without the scheme's support. Empaneled dialysis centers are available in all district headquarters and most major towns across Andhra Pradesh, reducing the need for long-distance travel for this recurring treatment.

how_to_apply.title: Check if you're already enrolled
how_to_apply.description: White ration card holders are automatically eligible. Visit ysraarogyasri.ap.gov.in or call 104 with your ration card number to check your status.

how_to_apply.title: If not enrolled - visit nearest government hospital or Aarogyasri center
how_to_apply.description: Bring your ration card (white or pink), Aadhaar card, and income proof. The Aarogyasri counter staff will verify your eligibility in the system.

how_to_apply.title: Submit documents for registration
how_to_apply.description: If eligible, provide your ration card, Aadhaar, and a passport photo. Registration is typically processed on the spot at government hospitals.

how_to_apply.title: Receive Aarogyasri Health Card
how_to_apply.description: You'll get an Aarogyasri card or digital confirmation. Keep this safe - you'll need it every time you seek treatment at an empanelled hospital.

how_to_apply.title: Use at any empanelled hospital across AP
how_to_apply.description: Present your Aarogyasri card and Aadhaar at any empanelled hospital in AP. The hospital handles the rest - verification, pre-authorization, and billing directly with the Trust.

important_alert.text: Always verify hospital empanelment before planned treatment. Non-empanelled hospitals cannot bill the Aarogyasri Trust, and you'll have to pay out of pocket. Check at ysraarogyasri.ap.gov.in or call 104. For emergencies, go to the nearest government hospital - all government hospitals in AP are empanelled.

faqs.question: I have Ayushman Bharat. Do I still need Aarogyasri?
faqs.answer: If you're in AP with income below ₹5 lakh, you likely qualify for both. Having both gives you ₹10 lakh combined annual coverage. Hospitals can bill either scheme depending on which covers the procedure. There's no downside to having both.

faqs.question: Do I need to pay anything at the hospital?
faqs.answer: Nothing. Treatment is completely cashless at empanelled hospitals. If any hospital demands payment from you for a covered procedure, report it immediately to the 104 helpline. The hospital settles everything directly with the Trust.

faqs.question: What if my bill exceeds ₹5 lakh?
faqs.answer: Aarogyasri covers up to ₹5 lakh per year. If your treatment costs more (rare for single procedures), the excess is your responsibility - unless you also have Ayushman Bharat, in which case the overflow can be covered under that scheme (additional ₹5L).

faqs.question: Can I use Aarogyasri outside Andhra Pradesh?
faqs.answer: No. Aarogyasri is AP-specific and works only at empanelled hospitals within the state. For treatment outside AP, use your Ayushman Bharat card instead (if you have one), as that's a national scheme.

faqs.question: Is emergency treatment covered without pre-authorization?
faqs.answer: Yes. In emergencies, go to the nearest empanelled or government hospital immediately. Treatment starts right away. Pre-authorization is sought by the hospital afterward. Never delay emergency care for paperwork.

faqs.question: How do I check my eligibility or Aarogyasri card status?
faqs.answer: Visit ysraarogyasri.ap.gov.in → use 'Check Eligibility' with your ration card number. Or call 104. The fastest way: visit any empanelled hospital's Aarogyasri counter with your ration card - they'll check on the spot.

faqs.question: My family member needs dialysis. Is it covered?
faqs.answer: Yes. Renal dialysis is covered under Aarogyasri's renal care category. Multiple dialysis sessions can be authorized within the ₹5 lakh annual limit. Pre-authorization is required for planned dialysis schedules. Visit an empanelled hospital with your Aarogyasri card.

faqs.question: What if the hospital I want to go to is not empanelled?
faqs.answer: Treatment at non-empanelled hospitals is NOT covered. You'll pay full costs yourself. Before planned treatment, always verify empanelment at ysraarogyasri.ap.gov.in or call 104. For emergencies, go to the nearest government hospital - all are empanelled.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for YSR Aarogyasri?
faqs.answer: All families with annual income below ₹5 lakh in Andhra Pradesh are eligible. White ration card holders are automatically enrolled. The family must have an Aarogyasri Health Card issued by the AP government. Apply through village/ward secretariat or Mee Seva centers with ration card, Aadhaar, and family photo.

faqs.question: Can I use YSR Aarogyasri outside Andhra Pradesh?
faqs.answer: Yes. YSR Aarogyasri is valid at empanelled hospitals across India - including major hospitals in Hyderabad, Chennai, Bangalore, and Delhi. Over 1,400 hospitals are empanelled nationwide. Check the hospital list at aarogyasri.telangana.gov.in or call the helpline 104 before travelling for treatment.
